```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## 1. What this document does

This compares two SIR BiLSTM calibrators:

- **Pretrained**: the original model shipped with the package (`pretrained_sir_calibrator()`),
  trained on about 60,000 simulations.
- **New**: a model trained here with the package's own trainer (`train_bilstm_calibrator()`),
  using the same simulator, the same parameter ranges and the same network size.

Both use the same post-processing: `ptran` and `R0` come from the network and
`crate = R0 * recov / ptran`.

The comparison has two parts:

1. **Simulated test curves** with known parameters, so accuracy can be measured directly.
2. **Real Utah COVID-19 data**: each model's estimates are used to reconstruct the epidemic
   curve, which is then compared with the observed cases.

Known differences between the two models, besides the new model's smaller training bank:

- The pretrained model divides daily cases by 10,000 before they enter the network; the
  package trainer divides by 100,000.
- The pretrained model uses separate output activations for each parameter; the package
  trainer uses one sigmoid for all scaled outputs.

## 2. Settings

```{r settings}
library(epiworldRcalibrate)

N_SIMS    <- params$n_sims   # training simulations for the new model
EPOCHS    <- params$epochs
N_TEST    <- params$n_test   # simulated test curves for the accuracy comparison
N_REPS    <- params$n_reps   # simulations per model for the real-data reconstruction
MODEL_DIR <- params$model_dir
SEED      <- 122

known_names  <- c("n", "recov")
target_names <- c("ptran", "crate", "R0")

data.frame(
  setting = c("training simulations", "epochs", "test curves", "reconstruction runs", "model folder"),
  value   = c(N_SIMS, EPOCHS, N_TEST, N_REPS, normalizePath(MODEL_DIR, mustWork = FALSE))
)
```

## 3. Train and save the new model

The model is saved in `MODEL_DIR`. If a trained model is already there, it is reused, so
re-knitting this document does not retrain unless `retrain: true` is set.

```{r train}
if (isTRUE(params$retrain) || !file.exists(file.path(MODEL_DIR, "model.pt"))) {
  train_bank <- generate_sir_training_data(n_sims = N_SIMS, ndays = 60, seed = SEED)

  train_time <- system.time(
    train_bilstm_calibrator(
      name           = "sir",
      known_names    = known_names,
      target_names   = target_names,
      type           = "SIR",
      data           = train_bank,
      output_dir     = MODEL_DIR,
      epochs         = EPOCHS,
      seed           = SEED,
      physics_weight = 0.03
    )
  )
  cat("Training took", round(train_time[["elapsed"]] / 60, 1), "minutes\n")
} else {
  cat("Using the saved model in", MODEL_DIR, "\n")
}

pretrained_cal <- pretrained_sir_calibrator()
new_cal        <- bilstm_calibrator(MODEL_DIR, known_names, type = "SIR")
```

Validation results written by the trainer (20% of the training bank held out):

```{r validation}
knitr::kable(
  read.csv(file.path(MODEL_DIR, "validation_metrics.csv")),
  digits = 3, caption = "New model: validation metrics"
)

history <- read.csv(file.path(MODEL_DIR, "training_history.csv"))
matplot(
  history$epoch, history[, c("train_loss", "validation_loss")], type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2,
  col = c("black", "red"), xlab = "epoch", ylab = "loss", main = "New model: training history"
)
legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = c("black", "red"), legend = c("train", "validation"))
```

## 4. Part A: simulated test curves

Fresh curves, simulated with a different seed from the training bank, so neither model has
seen them.

```{r test-set}
test_bank <- generate_sir_training_data(n_sims = N_TEST, ndays = 60, seed = 2025)

estimate_all <- function(cal) {
  out <- t(sapply(seq_len(N_TEST), function(i) {
    calibrate(
      as.numeric(test_bank$observations[i, ]), cal,
      n = test_bank$theta$n[i], recov = test_bank$theta$recov[i]
    )[target_names]
  }))
  as.data.frame(out)
}

pred_pretrained <- estimate_all(pretrained_cal)
pred_new        <- estimate_all(new_cal)
truth           <- test_bank$theta[, target_names]
```

```{r test-metrics}
accuracy <- function(pred, model) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(target_names, function(p) {
    err <- pred[[p]] - truth[[p]]
    data.frame(
      model     = model,
      parameter = p,
      MAE       = mean(abs(err)),
      RMSE      = sqrt(mean(err^2)),
      R2        = 1 - sum(err^2) / sum((truth[[p]] - mean(truth[[p]]))^2)
    )
  }))
}

test_metrics <- rbind(accuracy(pred_pretrained, "Pretrained"), accuracy(pred_new, "New"))
test_metrics <- test_metrics[order(test_metrics$parameter, test_metrics$model), ]
knitr::kable(test_metrics, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Accuracy on simulated test curves (lower MAE/RMSE and higher R2 are better)")
```

```{r test-plots, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (m in c("Pretrained", "New")) {
  pred <- if (m == "Pretrained") pred_pretrained else pred_new
  for (p in target_names) {
    plot(truth[[p]], pred[[p]], pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = adjustcolor("black", 0.4),
         xlab = paste("true", p), ylab = paste("estimated", p), main = paste(m, "-", p))
    abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)
  }
}
par(op)
```

How close are the two models to each other on the same curves?

```{r test-agreement}
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    parameter        = target_names,
    correlation      = sapply(target_names, function(p) cor(pred_pretrained[[p]], pred_new[[p]])),
    mean_abs_diff    = sapply(target_names, function(p) mean(abs(pred_pretrained[[p]] - pred_new[[p]])))
  ),
  digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Pretrained vs. new estimates on the same test curves"
)
```

## 5. Part B: real Utah COVID-19 data

The last 61 days of Utah daily cases.

```{r utah-data}
fetch_utah_covid_data <- function(n_days = 61) {
  zip_url <- "https://coronavirus-dashboard.utah.gov/Utah_COVID19_data.zip"
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
  download.file(zip_url, tmp, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  target <- grep(
    "Trends_Epidemic", unzip(tmp, list = TRUE)$Name,
    ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE
  )[1]
  daily <- read.csv(unz(tmp, target))
  unlink(tmp)
  daily$Date <- as.Date(daily$Date)
  daily <- daily[order(daily$Date), ]
  tail(daily, n_days)
}

utah     <- fetch_utah_covid_data(61)
observed <- utah$Daily.Cases
cat("Dates:", format(min(utah$Date)), "to", format(max(utah$Date)), "\n")
summary(observed)
```

Both models get the same known values. `n` and `recov` match the pretrained model's
assumptions; `preval` is taken from the first observed day.

```{r utah-estimates}
known <- list(n = 5000, recov = 1 / 7, preval = observed[1] / 5000)

est_pretrained <- calibrate(observed, pretrained_cal, n = known$n, recov = known$recov)
est_new        <- calibrate(observed, new_cal,        n = known$n, recov = known$recov)

knitr::kable(
  rbind(Pretrained = est_pretrained[target_names], New = est_new[target_names]),
  digits = 4, caption = "Estimates on the Utah data"
)
```

### Reconstructing the epidemic curve

For each model, simulate the SIR model `N_REPS` times with its estimates (different random
seeds each time) and summarise the daily cases by the median and a 95% interval.

```{r utah-reconstruct}
sim <- sir_simulator(ndays = 60)

reconstruct <- function(est) {
  curves <- t(sapply(seq_len(N_REPS), function(i) {
    sim$run(parameters = c(known, as.list(est[c("ptran", "crate")])), seed = i)
  }))
  list(
    median = apply(curves, 2, median),
    lower  = apply(curves, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
    upper  = apply(curves, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
  )
}

recon <- list(Pretrained = reconstruct(est_pretrained), New = reconstruct(est_new))
```

```{r utah-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
day <- seq_along(observed)
ylim <- range(c(observed, unlist(lapply(recon, function(r) c(r$lower, r$upper)))))

op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (m in names(recon)) {
  r <- recon[[m]]
  plot(day, r$median, type = "n", ylim = ylim, xlab = "day", ylab = "daily cases",
       main = paste(m, "model: observed vs. reconstructed"))
  polygon(c(day, rev(day)), c(r$upper, rev(r$lower)),
          col = adjustcolor("red", alpha.f = 0.3), border = NA)
  lines(day, r$median, col = "red", lwd = 2)
  lines(day, observed, col = "blue", lwd = 2)
  points(day, observed, col = "blue", pch = 16, cex = 0.6)
  legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = c("red", "blue"),
         legend = c("median (95% interval)", "observed"))
}
par(op)
```

Coverage is the share of observed days inside the 95% interval (close to 95% is good). RMSE
and MAE compare the median curve with the observed cases.

```{r utah-metrics}
fit_metrics <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(recon), function(m) {
  r <- recon[[m]]
  data.frame(
    model           = m,
    coverage_pct    = mean(observed >= r$lower & observed <= r$upper) * 100,
    RMSE            = sqrt(mean((r$median - observed)^2)),
    MAE             = mean(abs(r$median - observed))
  )
}))
knitr::kable(fit_metrics, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Reconstruction of the Utah curve")
```

## 6. How to read the results

- **Part A** answers "is the new model as accurate as the pretrained one?" Compare the MAE,
  RMSE and R2 of the two models for each parameter.
- **Part B** answers "does it give the same answer on real data?" Compare the two rows of
  estimates, and whether the reconstructed curves fit the observed cases equally well.
- If the new model is clearly worse, the likely causes are the smaller training bank
  (`r format(N_SIMS, big.mark = ",")` vs. about 60,000 simulations) and the different
  scaling of the daily cases (100,000 vs. 10,000).
